Lessons.Title: Equivalent Multiplication Expressions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: You will write equivalent expressions for the multiplication of a whole number and a unit fraction and explain the equivalence.
Key idea: A single fraction can be expressed by several equivalent whole-number-times-fraction multiplication expressions.
How to reason: Find a unit fraction or non-unit fraction factor that yields the required total.
Source-inspired opening: Warm-up: How Many Do You See? (10 minutes). Use the teacher-provided mathematical representations and explain how different valid answers arise.

Activity 1: Complete the Equations (15 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\frac{12}{5} =12 \times\underline{\hspace{.5in}}\), \(\frac{12}{5} =6 \times\underline{\hspace{.5in}}\), \(\frac{12}{5} =4 \times\underline{\hspace{.5in}}\), \(\frac{12}{5} =3 \times\underline{\hspace{.5in}}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 2: Fractions and Matching Expressions (20 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(6 \times \frac{1}{10}\), \(2 \times 4 \times \frac{1}{9}\), \(4 \times \frac{1}{5}\), \( 3 \times 2 \times \frac{1}{10}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.
Original source Cool-down is access-restricted/unverified; Edulytics substitutes goal-aligned independently authored teacher-reviewed exit prompt.
